# Cairn

> Cairn (npm: `cairn-engine`) is an open source agentic testing engine by Poem. You describe a browser task in plain language; Cairn uses AI to discover the steps once, freezes them as a JSON file, and replays that file on every later run without calling a model. When repair is explicitly enabled, Cairn attempts to repair a changed step with AI and saves the updated path only after verification. Application defects remain failures.

Landing page: https://team-poem.github.io/cairn-engine/ (English)
Korean landing page: https://team-poem.github.io/cairn-engine/ko/

## What it does
- Discover: turn a task description into concrete browser actions (log in, add to bag, open the cart) and save them as `*.skill.json`.
- Freeze: keep the path that worked so the next run follows the same steps.
- Replay: run the saved path deterministically. Basic replay makes no model calls, so it is cheap and stable in CI.
- Heal: opt-in AI repair for UI changes; save the updated path only after verification. Missing evidence in custom checks can be inconclusive and is not a pass.

## Architecture
A five-stage pipeline — Context, Plan, Execute, Judge, Report — where anything that varies comes in through a port:
- ContextProvider: gathers what the run should know (intent now; git diff, ticket, or docs later).
- Planner: turns intent into a Scenario. A static planner replays a frozen file; an LLM loop discovers a new one.
- SkillStore: where frozen `*.skill.json` files live (a folder by default, or your own store).
- Driver: drives the browser and waits for the page to settle. Chrome DevTools ships; bring Playwright or your own.
- Critic: decides pass or fail from three layers of evidence — execution, perception, logic — not a screenshot guess.
- Reporter: sends the result anywhere: console, JSON, or your team's tracker.

## Install
- `npm install -g cairn-engine`
- `cairn discover "log in, add a daypack, and open the cart" --url=https://your.app --freeze=cart.skill.json`
